# OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google

Lucas Ropek

10:49 AM PST · November 10, 2026

[](

In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses.

On Tuesday, the company rolled out a Business Hub that will serve as a place where companies can create business profiles that — in a feature that greatly resembles the kind of profiles that Google and other search engines already offer — allow enterprises to verify and update information about their products and services. The feature is currently in beta. [...] Eligible companies will also be able to create and launch a specialized business agent, which gives ChatGPT users the ability to ask questions about the business and its products.

“As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI,” the company said on Tuesday. “Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT.”

In a move that calls to mind Google’s Analytics, the Business Hub will also give users access to limited business insights. These insights will reveal how ChatGPT users interact with their products — including profile views, business mentions, website clicks, and other metrics.

results.content:
Photo: Adobe Stock

OpenAI just did something that belongs on every business owner’s radar, even though it got buried under a hundred other AI headlines this week. It launched a set of tools that let businesses manage their presence inside ChatGPT. There’s a new Business Hub where you can claim and verify your company’s profile, update your details, upload your products and pricing, and see how often ChatGPT is actually mentioning you. Eligible businesses can even build customer-facing AI agents that answer questions and help people buy. [...] The smart move is to audit how you actually show up in AI answers right now, today, because most business owners have never once checked. Open ChatGPT, ask it the questions your customers would ask to find a business like yours, and see what comes back. If you’re not mentioned, or the AI gets your details wrong, that’s your new blind spot. And just like the early days of SEO and social media, the businesses that move first will win this cheaply, while everyone else is still pretending it isn’t happening.

## This doesn’t kill Google. It adds a place you now have to show up [...] Read that again, because it quietly confirms something. ChatGPT is becoming a place where your customers find you, size you up, and get pointed toward one option. And OpenAI just handed you a dashboard to manage how you show up there. If that sounds familiar, it’s because it’s essentially a Google Business Profile for the AI era, and the race to claim your spot has already started.
